edges.effect_quant: Coffee is one of the more consistent food exposures associated with lower endometrial-cancer risk, with dose-response analyses suggesting that more intake generally means less risk.
edges.mechanism: Coffee may influence endometrial-cancer risk through improved insulin sensitivity, lower circulating estrogen availability, and metabolic effects that matter more in hyperinsulinemic or higher-BMI states. The stronger inverse associations in some postmenopausal and higher-BMI subgroups fit that mechanism reasonably well.
edges.summary: This is a steadier signal than many diet-cancer stories. Across successive meta-analyses, higher coffee intake is repeatedly linked to lower endometrial-cancer risk, and dose-response models show the association strengthening as consumption rises.
edges.caveats: The evidence is observational, so residual confounding cannot be eliminated. Still, the consistency across cohorts and case-control studies makes this one of the more credible dietary associations in the Track 2 set.

evidence.citation: JeY et al 2012 Int J Cancer
evidence.notes: Coffee consumption and risk of endometrial cancer: findings from a large up-to-date meta-analysis.
Coffee Decreases the Risk of Endometrial Cancer: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Prospective Cohort Studies.
